newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea won closes up on expected month-end demand.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea won closes up on expected month-end demand.

text.p: The won closed higher against the dollar on Monday although dollar short-covering in late trading erased part of its earlier gains, dealers said.
Expectation of large month-end export negotiations in coming days was behind the rise today, they said.
The won stood at 818.10 at the closing against the opening and the intraday low of 818.50. It touched a high of 817.00.
The court sentencing of two former presidents on charges of treason, sedition and corruption and business moguls on bribery had no impact on the foreign exchange market, dealers said.
"Banks sold dollars heavily in the morning ahead of the month's end," said a dealer at Korea First Bank.
"But dollar hedge buying from foreign banks, dollar short-covering and stop-loss buying covered much of earlier losses."
A range of 817 to 819 is seen for Tuesday with the base mid-rate at around 817.60, traders said. Today's mid-rate was pegged at 818.30.
